To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of premature mortality is particularly evident in people who gain weight and remain physically inactive, and that people who remain physically active, irrespective of their weight status, have the lowest risk of mortality.
Long-term changes in weight and leisure-time inactivity are both associated with an increased risk of premature mortality.
“People who gained weight while remaining inactive had the highest risk of premature mortality.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between body weight and physical inactivity and their impact on premature mortality.
the interplay between body weight and leisure time physical activity over a ~ 10 year period in relation to mortality in a general population.
the long-term changes in physical activity and body weight in relation to all cause and cardiovascular mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
weight gain and inactivity together are a bad combination, but that inactivity is a bigger factor in premature mortality than weight gain.
physical activity is the main factor in preventing premature mortality, and that weight gain is the main factor that can increase mortality risk among physically inactive persons.
weight gain and long-term inactivity are associated with increased risk of premature mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of maintaining a healthy body weight and being physically active throughout the adult life is important for a healthy life.
the combination of weight gain with physical inactivity is a particularly important risk factor for premature mortality.
long-term weight gain is associated with an increased mortality risk, especially among those who are physically inactive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to remain active, regardless of weight gain.
it is important to be physically active regardless of body weight, and that people should try to avoid weight gain, especially if they are inactive.
it is important to be physically active and maintain a healthy weight to reduce the risk of premature death from cardiovascular diseases.
